dct_description_sm: The RADARSAT-1 Antarctic Mapping Project (RAMP) was a collaboration between the Canadian Space Agency, NASA (Pathfinder Program and Polar Oceans and Ice Sheets Program), and the US National Science Foundation (Office of Polar Programs) to map the continent of Antarctica using the Canadian RADARSAT-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) in two missions. The RADARSAT-1 C-band SAR, operational from 1995 to 2013, was capable of acquiring high resolution (25 m) images of Earth's surface day or night, under all weather conditions. The second RAMP mission, the Modified Antarctic Mapping Mission (MAMM), captured imagery north of 80S up to the Antarctic coast, in both ascending and descending orbits. The objective of this mission was to observe changes in the ice sheet from the 1997 AMM-1 dataset and to use the multiple acquisitions to estimate the surface velocity of target areas of the ice sheet, providing benchmarks for gauging changes of Antarctica's ice cover. Along with the first RAMP mission, data collection, processing, and initial distribution were completed by the Alaska SAR Facility, Canadian government ground stations at Gatineau and Prince Albert, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and the Vexcel Corporation of Boulder, Colorado. The Ohio State University directed the overall project and scientific activities.
dct_title_s: Antarctica Satellite Mosaics and Tiles from the RADARSAT-1 Antarctic Mapping Project (RAMP) MAMM, Ascending Orbits, 2000
